requirements.requirement: bin/install-report works when invoked by POSIX /bin/sh.
requirements.summary: The rewritten installer uses POSIX shell constructs, passes /bin/sh syntax checking, and successfully executes through /bin/sh before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Installation supports destination paths containing spaces, preserves both supplied templates, and creates an executable launcher.
requirements.summary: Installation into a spaced path succeeded; direct comparisons and matching hashes establish intact template and launcher contents, and run-report had mode 755 and executed successfully.
The installer was run twice consecutively against the same destination, after which all files remained correct and the launcher worked.

requirements.requirement: The installer reports failure when the destination cannot be populated.
requirements.summary: Using an existing regular file as the destination produced a mkdir diagnostic and installer exit status 1.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged across execution and restart. No package or replacement-software installation occurred, and final dpkg health was clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node restart protocol is strong: it records a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, connection interruption, a different post-restart boot identity, a running system, unchanged bundle hashes, and working installer output. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart. The only notable hygiene issue is an unremoved /var/tmp verification installation.
limitations: The post-restart command reran the installer before comparing the /var/tmp destination, so it does not independently prove that those particular installed copies survived the reboot unchanged. It does directly show that the modified source bundle persisted and remained functional.

The lifecycle temporary-file inventory covers /tmp but not /var/tmp; retention of the /var/tmp proof directory is inferred from its presence in the final executor command and the absence of any later cleanup command.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing actions had clear roles: the installer edit implemented the task; temporary installations exercised required behavior; and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. The /tmp test directory and blocked file created by cmd-bde437e421e640d5 and cmd-b75c888c2d614442 were gone after reboot. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. The hygiene defect is the retained test installation under /var/tmp created by cmd-0c69c77ef06841e5 and repopulated by cmd-ba6965b899c94dc8; it supported restart evidence but no cleanup was captured. Final observations show no failed services, damaged package state, or new unsafe listener.
